question.text: A mid-sized corporate wants to participate in exchange-traded interest rate derivatives. The company has no existing exchange membership. What steps must it take to participate?

answer.text: Open a trading account with a trading member of the currency derivatives/IRD segment, complete KYC/UCC and required derivative financial documentation, and trade through the broker subject to applicable limits and regulator conditions
Apply directly to the exchange for membership and start trading
Obtain RBI permission and then approach any bank for execution
Corporates are not allowed to participate in ETIRD

explanation.text: The Logic: ETIRD clients, including corporate entities, trade through a trading member of the relevant exchange segment after opening an account. The workbook requires KYC, UCC and the derivative-segment financial documentation before trading. The Trap: Direct exchange membership remains possible only by meeting member eligibility criteria, so the typical corporate route is via a trading member rather than direct membership. RBI permission is not the gating step for the client route. Note: Corporates ordinarily participate as clients through a registered trading member, subject to applicable position limits and regulator conditions.
